rows.name: confluent terminating repair contract
rows.statement: Declared repair moves close every covered local mismatch, overlapping moves complete to a common local diamond on the quotient, and every accepted nontrivial aggregate transaction strictly lowers one declared well-founded exact measure, so repair reduction terminates and normal endpoints from sources with equal protected observation agree exactly when the observation identifies consistent states. The contract is declared through the rows repair_completeness, local_diamond, and strict_well_founded_transactional_descent in claims/assumption_dictionary.md; the endpoint-uniqueness characterization is machine-checked in Lean/ObservableNormalForms/ObservableNormalForms/ObserverConfluence.lean.
rows.notes: Promotion is a recorded basis amendment of the shape specified in docs/CANONICAL_REPAIR_LAW_RFC.md and requires a basis-wide dependency and countermodel review.

rows.name: algebra-state representation of public records
rows.statement: Public records are represented as the span of the mutually orthogonal projectors of a projective partition inside a finite complex matrix star algebra, with states read through the trace pairing and record events using that declared algebraic readout surface. The representation is packaged in Lean/EventAlgebra/PublicRecordAlgebra.lean and declared as declared_record_surface in claims/assumption_dictionary.md.
rows.notes: Promotion would state the algebra-state readout surface as a basis clause; a source-produced representation theorem would retire the row instead.

rows.name: operational effect additivity
rows.statement: A public frame valuation is additive on every required coexistent effect sum, v(A + B) = v(A) + v(B) whenever A + B remains an effect, across measurement contexts. With this additivity the finite Busch-Gleason theorem in Lean/EventAlgebra/FiniteBuschGleason.lean forces the Born trace form; the same module carries the countermodel in which positivity, per-context normalisation, and continuity hold while cross-context additivity fails, and the row source_produced_public_effect_algebra_deferred in claims/assumption_dictionary.md records that the retained finite unsharp web admits a transverse cubic non-Born valuation.
rows.notes: Removal needs a source-produced complex-tomographically-complete effect and instrument system with an operational theorem deriving noncontextual additivity on all required coexistent sums; lane #730 owns that scientific obligation.

rows.name: phase-operation instrument
rows.statement: The phase operation completing the diagonal record algebra to full operator tomography is a declared instrument: the exact lift I/2 - (2*sqrt(3)/3)*i*(QP - PQ) generates the missing Pauli-Y projector and is tomographically complete on fixed-trace two-by-two matrices, while the producer supplies no phase operation, rotated or phase outcome receipts, common-preparation validation, or operational effect composition. The lift and its boundary are declared in code/born_context_phase_lift/README.md and in the row source_phase_sensitive_instrument_deferred of claims/assumption_dictionary.md.
rows.notes: Removal needs a source-produced phase-sensitive instrument with rotated and phase outcome receipts and operational effect composition; the algebraic lift alone is the declared adapter.

rows.name: counting path reference
rows.statement: The path-space reference is a supplied initial law times the uniform-step counting weight; among row-stochastic kernels this normal form is characterized by invariance under independent relabeling of transition targets at fixed source, by row-constant weight, or by constant log-transition step action, and Axiom 3 selects neither the counting reference nor the trivial datum whose conditional resampling realizes it. The reference is formalized in Lean/InformationProjection/LogTransitionAction.lean; Lean/InformationProjection/ReferenceNormalForm.lean proves the characterization, and Lean/InformationProjection/SourceReferenceSelection.lean proves the counting-reference realization and the non-selection boundary.
rows.notes: Removal needs a source rule selecting the counting reference and the trivial datum; the relabeling-invariant normal form is characterized, and the selection remains open scientific work in lane #731.

rows.name: real Legendre enrichment
rows.statement: The finite source law fixes its four-corner log-transition action and a bilinear real extension that is affine in the velocity slot; adding (a/2)*y*(y - 1) for any a > 0 changes no realized source history and yields strictly convex Legendre-Hamilton systems that differ between values of a. Selecting one real velocity curvature is therefore a representation choice beyond the realized-history law, proved as a sharp finite no-go in Lean/Variational/RealizedHistoryLegendreNoGo.lean with the bridge itself in Lean/Variational/LegendreBridge.lean.
rows.notes: Removal needs additional source data or a physical receipt selecting the off-alphabet velocity curvature, which the realized-history law provably underdetermines. Mode-extremal consistency now pins the member uniquely within the registered one-parameter curvature family on the committed chain: interior-junction stationarity of the embedded constant-1 history forces a = 2*log(362055879/271780) > 0, with positivity equivalent to strict interior mode dominance (Lean/Variational/ModeExtremalEnrichment.lean). The selection principle is declared, references off-alphabet variations, and leaves the realized-history no-go in force; the row remains a representation choice.

rows.name: declared repair law: common faithful reference and repaired-visible fibre
rows.statement: One common faithful reference serves both Axiom 3 instantiations, and the transition feasible set is the fibre of the complete repaired visible datum of the active collar; on these two declared inputs the state projection selects the Gibbs exponential family and the transition projection selects weighted conditional resampling from the same reference, which yields the exact four-law package. The pair is declared through the row complete_repaired_visible_datum_fibre in claims/assumption_dictionary.md and consumed by Lean/Thermodynamics/FiniteConditionalRepair.lean; the B12 obstruction (code/thermodynamics/common_reference_obstruction/) and the B20 random-scan preflight (code/b20_random_scan/) prove that the pinned source run and its certified random-scan grammar do not supply the pair.
rows.notes: Promotion is the recorded axiomatization candidate of lane #732 with the B12/B20 bounded no-gos as its justification record; a simulator export realizing the law through the recorded-decision process would open the emergent rung.

rows.name: refinement-uniform low-temperature control
rows.statement: A declared refinement family carries minimum-preserving maps, one uniform positive energy-gap lower bound, and one cardinality bound, so the off-minimum Gibbs mass is controlled by cardBound * exp(-beta * gapBound) across every member simultaneously. The control and its negative control (a family with shrinking gaps violates the uniform conclusion) are proved in Lean/Thermodynamics/LowTemperatureControl.lean; the four-law falsifier row in claims/claim_registry.yaml names the refinement-uniform control as the receipt behind the continuum third-law reading.
rows.notes: Removal needs a source-produced refinement family whose uniform gap lower bound and cardinality bound are theorems rather than declared data. The refinement-uniform bound is now threaded into the composed four-law conclusion at the calibrated energy through the r0-member identification of the refinement attachment (fourLaws_composed).

rows.name: equal-face-weight and barycentric one-third port-dual rules
rows.statement: The port-dual measure places equal normalized weights on the twenty faces of the oriented carrier, and each face's weight is shared barycentrically, one third to each incident port, giving the normalized port-dual weight 1/12. The rules are declared in code/b14_jacobi/port_dual_metric_selector.certificate.json (declared_rules.face_weighting and declared_rules.vertex_share), with the measure pinned by the committed theorem in Lean/Screen/PrimitivePortDualMeasure.lean.
rows.notes: Promotion would fix the face weighting and barycentric share as a basis measure clause; a source derivation of the port-dual measure would retire the row.

rows.name: measure-to-metric and nearest-point repair rules
rows.statement: The normalized port-dual measure is read as the diagonal carrier inner product it induces on port functions, and the discriminator verdict is the nearest classified compact family in the functorially induced bracket-space metric. Both rules are declared in code/b14_jacobi/port_dual_metric_selector.certificate.json (declared_rules.measure_to_metric and declared_rules.repair_rule) and in the row carrier_induced_invariant_metric_class_and_nearest_point_rule of claims/assumption_dictionary.md; neither is source-derived.
rows.notes: Promotion would fix the induced-metric reading and the nearest-point verdict as basis repair semantics; a source derivation of either rule would retire the row.

rows.name: compact-Lie classification inputs
rows.statement: Three Lie-theory facts enter the gauge classification as declared classical inputs: the direct-sum splitting L = Z(L) + [L, L] of a compact Lie algebra into invariant submodules, surjectivity of the exponential map on compact connected groups, and the classification of compact simple Lie algebras through its dimension list. The cited modules declare the remaining Lie-theoretic bridge steps of the classification (centre rationality through the torus/cocharacter step, the su(2)^4 fixed-space exclusion, and the reductive-decomposition boundary bundle) as classical inputs subsumed under this row. They are marked as inputs in Lean/Screen/A5OPH.lean and Lean/Screen/TrichotomyCases.lean and cited by paper/deriving_standard_model_gauge_structure_from_observer_overlap_consistency.tex.
rows.notes: The facts are classical compact-Lie theory consumed as imports; the row's only movement is machine-checked replacements for the paper citations, and no derivation obligation attaches.

rows.name: matter candidate grammar
rows.statement: A matter candidate is a pair (S, M): S a stratum of the classified compact locus of the fourteen-parameter equivariant Jacobi variety on the twelve-port carrier, and M a nonempty Z/2-graded finite-dimensional complex module of the complexified semisimple bracket at S with zero abelian charges and total dimension at most twelve, counted up to graded isomorphism and the global parity flip. The grammar, budget, observables, and decision rule are frozen before any comparison in code/b15_matter_freeze/matter_class_freeze_v1.json; the exterior selection boundary is recorded as exterior_Higgs_matter_selection in claims/assumption_dictionary.md.
rows.notes: Removal needs a source-selection theorem that picks the physical matter module inside the frozen candidate class; grammar changes require a fresh freeze version before any evaluation.

rows.name: Koide balance premise
rows.statement: For a positive-chamber face circulant with square-root masses sqrt(m_k) = sqrt(s)*(a + 2*rho*cos(delta + 2*pi*k/3)), the balance premise rho/a = 1/sqrt(2) makes the signed Koide quotient equal 2/3 exactly. The circulant identity is machine-checked in Lean/ObserverPatchHolography/KoideCirculant.lean, and code/particles/leptons/koide_balance_comparison_certificate.py records the declared ancestry: the balance condition was abstracted from the measured charged triple, and no source-only derivation of the premise exists in the corpus.
rows.notes: Removal needs a source-only derivation of the balanced modulus rho/a = 1/sqrt(2); every Koide row is conditional with measured-target ancestry on the premise class.

rows.name: hadronic transport packet
rows.statement: The hadronic vacuum-polarization and spectral input is a pinned empirical payload built from the e+e- hadronic compilation registered in code/particles/hadron/empirical_ee_hadrons_sources.yaml (KNT19, arXiv:1911.00367, per docs/HADRON.md), consumed by the Ward-projected hadron lane and the alpha(m_Z) anchor transport as a flagged import. The registry carries a nonperturbative-QCD barrier policy: the payload is compare and transport data and is never promoted to a source-only theorem.
rows.notes: A source-side hadronic computation would replace the pinned payload; the packet is permanent as compare and transport data and is flagged wherever consumed.

rows.name: clock and energy calibration anchors
rows.statement: Internal modular charge, energy gaps, and repair-step order carry no laboratory units. PR-15 is the empirical attachment to declared measured clock and energy standards, including conversion into laboratory or SI units. It is separate from the source-side independent_physical_scale_receipt in claims/assumption_dictionary.md: that structural receipt asks two internally generated readouts to remove positive-rescaling freedom before any empirical unit conversion, and it is not part of this import row. The four-law claim in claims/claim_registry.yaml records laboratory energy and clock calibration as a named empirical input shared by the thermodynamics and constants lanes.
rows.notes: Laboratory-unit attachment is calibration against measured standards, so the row stays an import. It neither supplies nor replaces the separate source-generated scale-selection receipt.

rows.name: stable causality and open-image conditions
rows.statement: Stable causality of the constructed event region and the record-Cauchy global-hyperbolicity clause are named global assumptions, and the rank-four local charts of the event-manifold theorem carry an open-image receipt; no global causality claim is derived. Both are declared as record_cauchy_and_stable_causality and event_manifold_receipts_E1_E6 in claims/assumption_dictionary.md, with the synthetic receipt run in code/geometry/event_manifold_reconstruction.py.
rows.notes: Removal needs causal-structure and open-image theorems on the constructed event region in place of the named global assumptions; the spacetime and gravitation lanes own that composition work.

rows.name: proposed fundamental numerical parameters P and N
rows.statement: P and N are the two proposed fundamental free numerical parameters of the program. Measured calibration anchors, fitted inputs, comparison targets, and empirical transport payloads are separate numerical empirical inputs and remain flagged as such; other quantities are derived or imported mathematics. The screen-grain proposal P = phi + sqrt(pi)/A_T(P) has an interval-certified fixed point (docs/AXIOM_REFERENCE.md, certified under code/P_derivation/), and the direct capacity proposal N = log M_0(U_N), declared as declared_capacity_map in claims/assumption_dictionary.md, is not evaluable on the incomplete source antecedent.
rows.notes: The two numbers stay the only proposed fundamental free parameters under hard rule 2. Lane #736 records every empirical and mathematical input separately and never describes a result consuming those inputs as derived from P and N alone.

rows.name: spherically symmetric radial readout
rows.statement: A source distribution on the committed three-dimensional completion carrier is read through one radial strength profile: the flux through a shell depends on the shell radius alone. The premise enters as the strength field of RadialFluxData in Lean/Geometry/InverseSquareShellLaw.lean and is a symmetry declaration; no source theorem produces it.
rows.notes: Removal requires a source-derived isotropy statement for repair readback on the completion carrier.

Under it the inverse-square law is forced with the exponent supplied by the carrier dimension; no source theorem produces the normalization itself.
rows.notes: Removal requires a source-derived flux-conservation statement, for which the discrete Gauss receipts on the fixed carrier are the committed precursor.

The committed record derives the spatial generator; the second-order evolution shape enters as this declaration and no source theorem produces it. rows.notes: Removal needs a source theorem producing the second-order structure, for example a derivation of the first-order pairing from the repair and record architecture. Evidence context: transverse_wave_second_order; attainedCommittedOrderLaw_holds)

The chart scale is a declared coordinate; identifying a with a physical length and omega with a laboratory frequency consumes the clock and energy calibration anchors (PR-15). Carried as the fields chartScale, physicalFrequency, and physicalFrequency_sq_eq_symbol of LightSignalPremiseData.
rows.notes: Under the identification the composed surface proves the readout frequency equals the committed nonnegative branch, has an exact zero mode, and is globally one-Lipschitz in the chart momentum. Evidence context: physicalFrequency_zero_mode; physicalFrequency_global_one_lipschitz)

The package is a theorem on the finite thermodynamic model and a declared supply beyond it.

Evidence context: Lean/ObserverPatchHolography/EinsteinBranch/RegisterSurface.lean fields modularFlowData; entropyDifferentialIsModular; modularGeneratorSplit; centralChargeIsEdge; diamondKernelIdentification; finite-model discharge cited from Lean/Thermodynamics/EinsteinPremiseLink.lean via einstein_register_first_law_discharge

rows.name: layered shell-cardinality law
rows.statement: The layered readout graph has exactly shellCoeff * n^2 outward boundary edges at shell n for every positive layer index n up to a declared resolution depth. The premise enters as the shellCard field of LayeredFluxData in Lean/Screen/LayeredDiscreteGauss.lean; no source theorem produces it. The committed 20 * n^2 faceCount in Lean/Screen/DiscreteRefinement.lean is a subdivision count on one fixed screen; identifying subdivision frequency with radial layer distance is exactly the open step, so the count is declared rather than derived. The depth truncation is forced: unbounded_shellCard_forces_zero proves an n^2 law imposed at every positive layer collapses the coefficient to zero on any finite carrier.
rows.notes: Removal requires a layered carrier built from the committed refinement tower together with a derived boundary-edge count and a layer-to-distance identification.

rows.name: layered shell equidistribution
rows.statement: Within one shell of the layered readout graph, up to the declared depth, every outward boundary edge carries the same outward flux. The premise enters as the equidistributed field of LayeredFluxData in Lean/Screen/LayeredDiscreteGauss.lean and is the discrete counterpart of the spherically symmetric radial readout premise (PR-18); no source theorem produces it.

rows.statement: On the layered readout graph the vertex outflow of the flux field equals a declared source supported in the layer-zero ball, for every vertex up to the declared depth, so the flux is divergence-free outside the source region there. The premise enters as the steadyGauss and sourceSupport fields of LayeredFluxData in Lean/Screen/LayeredDiscreteGauss.lean. The depth truncation is forced: steady_total_source_eq_zero proves a steady drained source on the whole closed finite carrier has zero total load, so layers beyond depth absorb the flux in place of spatial infinity. On the fixed twelve-port carrier the corresponding identity is a theorem: steady_witness_regionFlux_eq_source derives it from the committed regional continuity law.
rows.notes: Removal requires a layered carrier realization carrying a steady continuity witness; the twelve-port bridge theorem records the discharge pattern.

rows.statement: The region system of the committed net is the four-region diamond bot < left, right < top with the region map assigning the scalar bottom, the two slot-factor algebras, and the full joint algebra, entering as the regionMap field of StructuralNetDeclaredPremises with committed instances twoSlotAlgebra (Lean/QFT/TwoSlotCPNetWitness.lean) and twoSlotAlgebra247 (Lean/QFT/SourceCorrelationCapstone.lean). No source theorem produces the region system.

For the support-disjoint pair (86, 247) the split is backed by the kernel-checked support disjointness theorem supports_disjoint; the split itself is declared, and the designated pair (86, 88) has overlapping supports with no disjointness receipt.

rows.name: same-source loop-to-kernel identity
rows.statement: The carrier loop classes realized by the source are the six-axis screen gluing classes of Lean/Screen/Z6Exact.lean, and their image under the committed intertwiner sixAxisToKernel of Lean/Screen/Z6Descent.lean (axis generator to the kernel generator (omega_3 I_3, -I_2, e^{i pi/3}), antipodal sign reversal to conjugation, injective with image exactly the tensor-action kernel) generates the full Z6 tensor-action kernel of Lean/Screen/TraceBalancedKernel.lean; the physical global gauge form is the quotient of SU(3) x SU(2) x U(1) by that image, S(U(3) x U(2))/Z6. The realized local weights descend through all four admissible quotients (Z6Descent.four_admissible_global_forms), so this identity is the clause that selects the physical quotient; the intertwiner itself is a proved receipt, and the premise is the same-source physical identification of its domain.
rows.notes: Removal needs a same-source holonomy theorem computing the carrier loop classes from the source packet and matching them to the kernel through the committed intertwiner; the companion character-category completeness residual remains open. Registration keeps OL-G2 conditional with the premise named.

rows.name: family band-selection rules: single complete faithful band and operational cost order
rows.statement: The family multiplicity object is a single complete spectral band of the twelve-port adjacency realized inside the screen coefficient space: candidates carrying a source-visible proper splitting projector are excluded (the single-complete-object clause), bands whose rotation action has nontrivial kernel are excluded (the faithfulness clause), and the complex dimension lies in the pinned physical window [3, 5]. Admissible candidates are compared by the operational Laplacian seam cost per unit norm over Z[sqrt5], and the unique strict minimizer is selected. On the committed carrier the admissible candidates are the 3, 3', and 5 bands with exact costs 5 - sqrt5 < 6 < 5 + sqrt5, so the rules select the rank-three band (Lean/Screen/A5FamilyBand.lean, family_band_selected); without the faithfulness clause the minimizer is the trivial band at cost zero (trivial_band_without_faithfulness), so the clause is load-bearing. The clauses are declared in code/a5_closure/family_band_attachment_certificate.py and its reference manifest.
rows.notes: Removal needs a source derivation of the comparison order and of the realization clause that places the multiplicity object inside the screen coefficient space; registration composes OL-G4 conditionally, and family triplication stays a selection under these rules.

rows.name: fine-structure closure map selection
rows.statement: The P-closure map consumed by the fine-structure lane is a declared selection: the one-loop running and matching conventions, the tree-level m_Z closure, and the continuation masses enter as declared map data, certified as declared in the interval contraction certificate, and no source rule selects this map among admissible closure maps.

rows.statement: The coherent charged-lepton kappa closure consumes one declared premise: the anchor gap is coherent with the pinned hadronic payload across the three charged channels, which narrows the certified rectangle intervals to the coherent intervals by the recorded factor.
rows.notes: Removal needs a source derivation of the payload-coherent anchor gap; every coherent-interval row is conditional on the premise and the rectangle intervals stand without it.

rows.statement: The conditional Higgs and top rows of the electroweak section consume declared selection premises; the postdiction ledger records the rows as conditional on the declared selection axioms, and the sector stance is owed.

rows.name: horizon record central-charge identification
rows.statement: Over the declared repair law (PR-07), the modular weight of the declared reference splits as -log ref = 2*pi*B + Z, with the central charge Z measurable through the repaired visible datum; the identification of B with a physical boost energy and of Z with the edge record of a physical horizon is content of the row. The 2*pi coefficient is the declared modular normalization of the split.

The composition with the repair kernel conserves the central charge with no further hypothesis, so the cap Clausius inequality carries no independent temperature input. No continuum horizon exists on the finite model; horizon temperature in physical units stays with PR-15 plus the horizon-dictionary content of this row. Evidence context: Lean/Thermodynamics/HorizonThermalitySurface.lean: structure HorizonRecordData; theorems HorizonSurface.horizon_cap_clausius; HorizonSurface.entanglement_first_law_exact; HorizonSurface.entanglement_first_law_first_order; HorizonSurface.modular_weight_double_identification

rows.name: pointwise-continuous public star-automorphism flow
rows.statement: A real-parameter group of star automorphisms of one represented finite matrix algebra is supplied, with identity at zero, the group law, and pointwise continuity. The finite Stone-converse receipt then represents that supplied flow by conjugation with a time-independent self-adjoint generator, unique up to an additive real scalar. The premise supplies neither a source-selected evolution nor a physical clock.
rows.notes: Removal needs the observer protocol to emit the automorphism group and its source-selected generator. Physical-time calibration remains a separate PR-15 attachment.

rows.name: finite subsystem split and normalized local-operation interface
rows.statement: The finite locality helpers are read on a supplied bipartite carrier split with a designated local factor and a normalized local operation: a row-normalized classical kernel or Kraus-complete quantum family. Adaptive variants additionally take a supplied scheduler and consultation region. These data yield exact algebraic no-signalling and dependency-cone identities but do not identify spacelike physical regions, a laboratory channel, or a source-selected factorization.
rows.notes: Removal needs a source-produced subsystem or region split, normalized channel semantics, and scheduler provenance. PR-52 separately owns the physical spacetime and causal reading.

rows.name: source-selected real variational dynamics and symmetry data
rows.statement: The variational surface is supplied with a positive initial law and transition kernel, a finite history length, a record embedding of the alphabet into the reals, a real Lagrangian or stiffness and potential with derivative data, and, for Noether transport, a differentiable one-parameter transformation and exact invariance law. The finite Euler-Lagrange, Legendre-Hamilton, and Noether receipts are conditional on these data and are stated for fixed-endpoint interior-junction variations; the observer source does not select them.
rows.notes: Removal needs one source-derived real history action, potential, symmetry action, and physical clock that compose with the path reference and real enrichment rather than merely standing beside them.

rows.name: physical global-form selection attachments
rows.statement: Selection of the physical global gauge group from the four quotients compatible with the realized local weights requires a source-complete character category, an instanton or topological normalization, and a laboratory flux or line-operator attachment. The finite kernel, six-axis intertwiner, and four-quotient menu do not supply those identifications.
rows.notes: Removal needs a same-source physical discriminator that selects one quotient and rules out the other three without importing the observed Standard Model global form.

rows.name: spacetime Spin and fermion-chirality attachment
rows.statement: The parity-graded exterior component table is attached to a physical Lorentzian Spin structure, odd-Weyl fermion typing, and fermion parity so that the finite table grading has the claimed spacetime chirality meaning. The central arithmetic and parity scan do not construct this attachment.
rows.notes: Removal needs a source-selected Lorentzian Spin lift that composes with the exterior matter carrier and its local dynamics.

rows.name: one-Higgs scalar carrier and kinetic-action attachment
rows.statement: One complex weak doublet of hypercharge one half is selected as the physical scalar carrier, identified with the declared weak block, and furnished with a gauge-covariant kinetic action and normalization. The exterior table and central-weight arithmetic identify a compatible candidate but do not select its physical existence or dynamics.
rows.notes: Removal needs a source action that selects the scalar carrier and fixes its kinetic normalization rather than assuming the one-Higgs branch.

rows.name: renormalizable Higgs potential and electroweak-breaking law
rows.statement: The scalar sector carries the renormalizable quadratic-plus-quartic Higgs potential, a stable symmetry-breaking branch, and a vacuum attachment with a declared relation to the physical electroweak scale. No committed OPH theorem selects the potential, its coefficients, or the broken vacuum.
rows.notes: Removal needs a target-clean source-derived stable scalar potential, vacuum, and scale bridge. Until then electroweak breaking is a registered premise, not an OPH result.

rows.name: Yukawa interaction-line and coupling-matrix attachment
rows.statement: The gauge-invariant up, down, and charged-lepton interaction lines are selected on the one-Higgs matter package and furnished with complete Yukawa matrices, including family labels and physical chiral attachment. The exterior grammar records compatible invariant lines, while exact non-identifiability receipts show that it does not determine their matrices, eigenvalues, textures, or phases.
rows.notes: Removal needs a source-derived interaction action selecting all three matrices without measured mass or mixing ancestry.

rows.name: common screen-electroweak load and capacity bridge
rows.statement: The A5-invariant screen-load line and the electroweak scalar order-unit line are identified by one refinement-natural positive unital readout, and that same typed load is attached to the global capacity action used by the conditional N closure. The current branch certificate explicitly leaves the common-load identification and inherited screen-electroweak bridge premises open.
rows.notes: Removal needs a target-independent same-quantity theorem and a source-derived global capacity action; registering the row licenses only conditional ancestry.

rows.name: observer-to-physical-spacetime and causal attachment
rows.statement: The intrinsic Lorentz module, null cone, event-germ atlas, and declared finite causal regions are jointly identified with one observer-produced physical spacetime, including compatible rods, operational clocks, causal reachability, refinement, and continuum soldering. The existing algebraic geometry and finite-net modules explicitly do not construct this joint attachment.
rows.notes: Removal needs one source-derived, refinement-compatible spacetime witness and explicit maps from the finite observer records to its causal and metric structure.

rows.name: physical finite-carrier propagation, frame, and comparison attachment
rows.statement: A named branch-indexed finite-carrier propagation action is identified with a physical photon or other declared field sector, a coherent frame and boost law, a calibrated clock and length scale, a cofinal gluing or continuum domain, and an operational wave-packet readout with nuisance and comparison semantics. The primitive-port rank-six and seam-current rank-two actions are distinct branches; their exact internal dispersion coefficients alone supply none of these attachments.
rows.notes: Removal needs a target-clean physical field/readout bridge. A predictive comparison remains ineligible until this row and the applicable frozen decision-rule and power requirements are met.

rows.name: source gauge-field, current, and action attachment
rows.statement: The selected compact bracket and matter representation are realized by one source-produced gauge connection, current algebra, field strength, covariant matter operator, and local action on the same spacetime carrier. The finite classification and invariant-form receipts determine conditional algebraic shapes but do not construct this physical field/action package.
rows.notes: Removal needs one observer-native gauge and matter action that composes with the spacetime, quantum, and calibration lanes; side-by-side classification theorems are insufficient.

rows.name: declared baryon- and lepton-number labels
rows.statement: The ten one-generation Weyl-field labels are furnished with the displayed accidental baryon number B and lepton number L. These labels are used to classify baryon-violating dimension-six field multisets and to state Delta B equals Delta L. Gauge representation and hypercharge data do not by themselves derive these two global labels or prove their conservation.
rows.notes: Removal needs a source-side definition of the accidental charges on the physical matter carrier. The finite census remains conditional on the displayed labels.

rows.name: dimension-six baryon-operator eligibility and contraction grammar
rows.statement: Candidate dimension-six baryon operators are represented by ordered four-field multisets on the declared one-generation Weyl table and filtered by exact hypercharge neutrality, color triality, weak parity, Lorentz-chirality parity, and nonzero baryon label. Surviving rows are tested in the supplied epsilon-contraction and exterior-algebra grammar. The exhaustive finite result proves completeness only inside this declared grammar.
rows.notes: Removal needs a source-derived effective-operator domain and a proof that the finite grammar is complete for the physical low-energy action.

rows.name: physical proton state and baryon-violating effective-action attachment
rows.statement: The declared quark and lepton fields, baryon labels, and finite operator census are attached to a physical proton state and one low-energy effective action with source-selected Wilson coefficients, renormalization and scale conventions, QCD matrix elements, and decay readout. Without this attachment the census neither proves proton stability nor predicts a lifetime.
rows.notes: Removal needs one common observer realization of the matter, QCD, and action construction plus an operational decay comparison. The current exact result is only a conditional finite operator census.

rows.name: net-compatible dynamics and region-symmetry action
rows.statement: No registered premise supplies a pointwise-continuous automorphism flow of the joint algebra that maps each regional algebra of the declared diamond to itself or to a covariant image, nor any group action on the region system beyond the constructed Z/2 slot swap. PR-43 supplies a flow on one full matrix block with no region compatibility, and PR-52 owns the physical time and causal reading. This row is the exact block on the OL-C6 time-slice target.
rows.notes: Removal needs a source-selected flow or symmetry action compatible with the declared regional net. The Z/2 slot-swap receipt on the equal-alphabet carrier is the first nonconstant region-symmetry action and does not discharge the dynamics half.
